repairs.before: Strongest feature: Ward carefully distinguishes the modest conclusion that physics makes underlying ontology a legitimate question from the much stronger conclusion that the hidden reality is God, using ordinary solidity, color, quantum theory, and eleven-dimensional strings to illustrate the appearance-reality separation. Principal limitation: those compressed examples support representational distance but neither mind-likeness nor the sweeping assertion that respectable physics uniformly endorses his characterization, while the unnamed physicist anecdote supplies no independently inspectable warrant. Live burden: he must add a discriminating inference showing why nonmental physical structure, mathematical description, or epistemic humility explains the separation less successfully than fundamental mentality. Locked score: 76 reflects strong coherence, direct setup, explicit calibration, and understandable relevance, tempered by underdocumented science, conceptual compression, and the acknowledged absence of any completed bridge from altered appearance to divinity.
